This evidence relies heavily on the extrapolation of current exponential growth in AI development and hardware advancements. There is no guarantee that these scaling laws will continue indefinitely, especially when transitioning from narrow AI to general intelligence. The 'low-hanging fruit' of current AI paradigms may soon be exhausted, and fundamental breakthroughs, which are inherently unpredictable and do not necessarily follow exponential trends, may be required. This constitutes a significant logical leap, ignoring potential plateaus or diminishing returns.

While this evidence claims to support the proposition, its own description highlights 'fundamental conceptual, philosophical, and cognitive science challenges inherent in defining and achieving true general intelligence, questioning current AI paradigms.' It is an unsupported assumption that these deeply complex, often intractable challenges will be adequately resolved and lead to widespread consensus within the next 24 years. The evidence likely understates the depth of these issues or assumes a definition of AGI that may not be universally accepted or truly 'general' by 2047.
